arxiv-2105-05980.title: DONet: Dual-Octave Network for Fast MR Image Reconstruction Thanks: C.-M. Feng and Y. Xu are with the Shenzhen Key Laboratory of Visual Object Detection and Recognition, Harbin Institute of Technology (Shenzhen), 518055, China. (Email: strawberry.feng0304@gmail.com; yongxu@ymail.com). (Corresponding
arxiv-2105-05980.creator: Chun-Mei Feng, Zhanyuan Yang, Huazhu Fu, Yong Xu
arxiv-2105-05980.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Chun-Mei Feng, Zhanyuan Yang, Huazhu Fu, Yong Xu. Magnetic resonance (MR) image acquisition is an inherently prolonged process, whose acceleration has long been the subject of research. This is commonly achieved by obtaining multiple undersampled images, simultaneously, through parallel imaging. In this paper, we propose the Dual-Octave Network (DONet), which is capable of learning multi-scale spatial-frequency features from both the real and imaginary components of MR data, for parallel fast MR image reconstruction.

arxiv-2108-13810.description: Abstract We consider the query recommendation problem in closed loop interactive learning settings like online information gathering and exploratory analytics. The problem can be naturally modelled using the Multi-Armed Bandits (MAB) framework with countably many arms. arxiv-2111-06274.title: Energy spreading, equipartition and chaos in lattices with non-central forces
arxiv-2111-06274.creator: Arnold Ngapasare, Georgios Theocharis, Olivier Richoux, Vassos Achilleos, Charalampos Skokos, Nonlinear Dynamics and Chaos GroupDepartment of Mathematics and Applied MathematicsUniversity of Cape Town, Rondebosch 7701, South Africa, Laboratoire d’Acoustique de l’Université du MansUMR CNRS 6613 Av. O
arxiv-2111-06274.description: Abstract We numerically study a one dimensional, nonlinear lattice model which in the linear limit is relevant to the study of bending (flexural) waves. In contrast with the classic one dimensional mass-spring system, the linear dispersion relation of the considered model has different characteristics in the low frequency limit.

arxiv-2201-00391.title: On the independence number of random trees via tricolourations
arxiv-2201-00391.creator: Etienne Bellin CMAP - Ecole Polytechnique
arxiv-2201-00391.description: Abstract We are interested in the independence number of large random simply generated trees and related parameters, such as their matching number or the kernel dimension of their adjacency matrix. We express these quantities using a canonical tricolouration, which is a way to colour the vertices of a tree with three colours.

arxiv-2209-13009.title: Can Existing Approaches Manage Dynamic and Large Business Processes enacted through Systems-of-Systems? Publication type: Review Article
arxiv-2209-13009.creator: Maria Istela Cagnin, Elisa Yumi Nakagawa
arxiv-2209-13009.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Maria Istela Cagnin, Elisa Yumi Nakagawa. In the era of joint ventures (JV) and mergers & acquisitions (M&A), dynamic and large business processes can emerge to achieve broader business goals and are often formed from business processes of distinct organizations. Software systems of such distinct organizations should support these larger processes and, for this, they need to communicate among them forming the so called Systems-of-Systems (SoS).

arxiv-2303-16117.title: Feature Engineering Methods on Multivariate Time-Series Data for Financial Data Science Competitions Thanks: Citation : Authors. Title. Pages…. DOI:000000/11111.
arxiv-2303-16117.creator: Thomas Wong, Mauricio Barahona
arxiv-2303-16117.description: Abstract We apply different feature engineering methods for time-series to US market price data. The predictive power of models are tested against Numerai-Signals targets. K eywords Machine Learning, Time-Series Prediction, 1 Introduction Financial data are often available in the form of time series. These time series are often highly dimensional with complex relationships between them.

arxiv-2304-10721.title: Pinch effect of self-generated magnetic fields in the quantum degenerate plasmas on the heating process of the double-cone ignition scheme
arxiv-2304-10721.creator: Y.-H. Li, D. Wu, J. Zhang
arxiv-2304-10721.description: Abstract In the double-cone ignition scheme, compressed fuels in two head-on cones are ejected to collide, forming a colliding plasma with an isochoric distribution for rapid heating by high flux fast electrons from picosecond petawatt laser beams in the perpendicular direction from the cone axis.

arxiv-2401-03891.title: Radius selection using kernel density estimation for the computation of nonlinear measures
arxiv-2401-03891.creator: Johan Medrano, Abderrahmane Kheddar, Annick Lesne, Sofiane Ramdani
arxiv-2401-03891.description: Abstract When nonlinear measures are estimated from sampled temporal signals with finite-length, a radius parameter must be carefully selected to avoid a poor estimation. These measures are generally derived from the correlation integral which quantifies the probability of finding neighbors, i.e. pair of points spaced by less than the radius parameter.

arxiv-2506-18286.title: Detailed Chemical Abundance Analysis of Metal-Poor Turn-Off Stars: One with [Fe/H] < − 4 <-4 and Three with [Fe/H] < − 3 <-3 .
arxiv-2506-18286.creator: Takuma Suda, Patrick François, Shinya Wanajo, Elisabetta Caffau, Wako Aoki, Piercarlo Bonifacio
arxiv-2506-18286.description: Abstract We present the analysis of four new extremely metal poor turn-off stars thanks to high-resolution spectra obtained with the Subaru/HDS spectrograph. We determined the abundances and upper limits of Li, C, Mg, Ca, Sr, and Ba. Metallicities range from [Fe/H] = − 3.3 =-3.3 to − 4.4 -4.4 dex.

arxiv-2512-05188.title: Thermal Damping of Mass-Modulating Scalars
arxiv-2512-05188.creator: Abhishek Banerjee ID, Ngan H. Nguyen ID, Erwin H. Tanin ID
arxiv-2512-05188.description: Abstract The cosmological evolution of a scalar field is shaped by Hubble damping. Any non-gravitational couplings of the scalar with the primordial thermal bath generically contribute additional damping. Although rarely considered, such thermal damping could be the dominant dissipative effect. We derive approximate but highly general thermal-damping rates of scalar fields that modulate the masses of thermally populated particles.

arxiv-2601-08225.title: User-Oriented Multi-Turn Dialogue Generation with Tool Use at scale
arxiv-2601-08225.creator: Jungho Cho, Minbyul Jeong, Sungrae Park
arxiv-2601-08225.description: Abstract The recent paradigm shift toward large reasoning models (LRMs) as autonomous agents has intensified the demand for sophisticated, multi-turn tool-use capabilities. Yet, existing datasets and data-generation approaches are limited by static, predefined toolsets that cannot scale to the complexity of open-ended human-agent collaboration.

arxiv-2601-09569.title: Dynamical Stabilization of Inverted Magnetization and Antimagnons by Spin Injection in an Extended Magnetic System
arxiv-2601-09569.creator: Emir Karadža, Hanchen Wang, Niklas Kercher, Paul Noël, William Legrand, Richard Schlitz, Pietro Gambardella
arxiv-2601-09569.description: Abstract Dynamical perturbations can modify the energy landscape of a physical system, such that unstable equilibrium configurations become stable when subject to an external drive. The magnetic analog of such dynamical stabilization corresponds to saturation of the magnetization against an external field.

arxiv-2602-11277.title: Fate of 𝜽 𝟏𝟐 \boldsymbol{\theta_{12}} under 𝝁 − 𝝉 \boldsymbol{\mu-\tau} Reflection Symmetry in Light of the First JUNO Results
arxiv-2602-11277.creator: Ranjeet Kumar
arxiv-2602-11277.description: Abstract The recent JUNO measurements of θ 12 \theta_{12} and Δ ​ m 21 2 \Delta m^{2}_{21} open a new avenue for probing flavor symmetric structures in the lepton sector. Motivated by this, we study a model in which μ − τ \mu-\tau reflection symmetry naturally emerges from an underlying A 4 A_{4} flavor symmetry within a type-II seesaw framework.

The data includes longitudinal characteristics with and without a horizontal tail as well as results of preliminary investigation of lateral-directional characteristics. The

pmc-10736954.title: SMART MUSIC INTERVENTION: PROTOCOL DEVELOPMENT OF A WEARABLE DEVICE FOR COLLECTION OF PHYSIOLOGICAL DATA
pmc-10736954.creator: Emily Ihara, Parth Pathak, Megumi Inoue, Catherine Tompkins, Y Alicia Hong
pmc-10736954.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). This study tested a protocol of collecting physiological data through sensors on a wearable device in response to favorite music from late adolescence/early adulthood. The benefits of personalized music for individuals living with dementia have been demonstrated in various studies, showing decreases in agitation, anxiety, depression, and other behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia and improvement in mood, memory, and well-being. Most studies have relied on observational data, standardized clinical scales, and self- or caregiver-reported perceptions of the effects of personalized music.

pmc-11391668.title: Routine Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI) measurement: a window into atherosclerosis and early left ventricular dysfunction in patients diagnosed with cancer
pmc-11391668.creator: Netanel Golan, Rafael Y. Brzezinski, Moaad Slieman, Shafik Khoury, Ofer Havakuk, Yan Topilsky, Shmuel Banai, Michal Laufer-Perl
pmc-11391668.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundCancer therapy is considered to cause accelerated ischemia. Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI) measurement is an inexpensive, simple, available test for the early diagnosis of peripheral artery disease (PAD); however, it is not performed routinely. We aimed to evaluate the role of routine ABI measurement for the diagnosis of PAD among patients diagnosed with cancer and whether it correlates with left ventricular (LV) dysfunction.MethodsA retrospective, single-center study including patients diagnosed with cancer at Tel Aviv Sourasky Medical Center.

pmc-11430211.title: New insights into honey bee viral and bacterial seasonal infection patterns using third-generation nanopore sequencing on honey bee haemolymph
pmc-11430211.creator: Cato Van Herzele, Sieglinde Coppens, Nick Vereecke, Sebastiaan Theuns, Dirk C de Graaf, Hans Nauwynck
pmc-11430211.description: Honey bees are rapidly declining, which poses a significant threat to our environment and agriculture industry. These vital insects face a disease complex believed to be caused by a combination of parasites, viruses, pesticides, and nutritional deficiencies. However, the real aetiology is still enigmatic.

pmc-11611726.title: Durable remission of refractory and advanced stage mycosis fungoides/sezary syndrome utilizing an “outpatient” alemtuzumab, fludarabine-based reduced intensity allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation
pmc-11611726.creator: Phuong Vo, Ramaprasad Srinivasan, Enkhtsetseg Purev, Emily McDuffee, Tatyana Worthy, Reem Shalabi, Kristen Wood, Brian Wells, Robert Reger, David Stroncek, Nancy Geller, Georg Aue, Xin Tian, Richard Childs
pmc-11611726.description: t Sezary syndrome (SS), the most prevalent subtypes of primary cutaneous T-cells lymphomas (CTCL), present significant treatment challenges in advanced stages. Currently, there is no treatment available for subjects with advanced disease that improves overall survival. Allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HCT) had been utilized for the treatment of MF/SS [1–3].

pmc-11671694.title: Predicting phage–host interactions via feature augmentation and regional graph convolution
pmc-11671694.creator: Ankang Wei, Zhen Xiao, Lingling Fu, Weizhong Zhao, Xingpeng Jiang
pmc-11671694.description: Identifying phage–host interactions (PHIs) is a crucial step in developing phage therapy, which is the promising solution to addressing the issue of antibiotic resistance in superbugs. However, the lifestyle of phages, which strongly depends on their host for life activities, limits their cultivability, making the study of predicting PHIs time-consuming and labor-intensive for traditional wet lab experiments.

pmc-12563039.title: Selective Endocytosis-Mediated Omicron S1-RBD Internalization Revealed by Reconstitution of ACE2-S1-RBD Interaction on Micropatterned Membrane Substrates
pmc-12563039.creator: Angelin M. Philip, S. M. Nasir Uddin, Zeyaul Islam, Prasanna R. Kolatkar, Kabir H. Biswas
pmc-12563039.description: The SARS-CoV-2 spike protein, through its receptor binding domain (S1-RBD), binds to the angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) receptor on the host cell membrane, leading to viral infection. Several mutations in S1-RBD in SARS-CoV-2 variants are known to enhance infection through an increased affinity for ACE2.

pmc-13188789.title: Transcriptome analysis identifies key miRNAs involved in the regulation of rabbit intramuscular fat deposition
pmc-13188789.creator: Guohua Song, Hui Wang, Zhuoya Jin, Qianting Duan, Ifeanyi S Ahamba, Shuhui Wang, Zhanjun Ren, Xianggui Dong
pmc-13188789.description: BackgroundIntramuscular fat (IMF) is a critical determinant of rabbit meat quality, influencing tenderness, juiciness, and flavor. miRNAs are crucial for IMF synthesis by regulating genes involved in lipid deposition, but the mechanisms by which miRNAs regulate IMF deposition in rabbits remain poorly understood.

pmc-13223822.title: Prospective Pilot Clinical Study of High-Purity Magnesium Plates and Screws for Le Fort I Osteosynthesis
pmc-13223822.creator: Wei-fa Yang, Pak Chuen Patrick Tai, Ling Qin, Yiu Yan Leung
pmc-13223822.description: ObjectivesThis prospective clinical study aimed to evaluate the feasibility, safety, and clinical performance of an innovative high-purity magnesium (HP-Mg) plate and screw system for internal fixation in orthognathic surgery.Materials and MethodsPatients indicated for orthognathic surgery fulfilling the study criteria were invited to participate.

pmc-13233517.title: Middle-Term Follow-Up Outcomes of the Customised Temporomandibular Joint-Skull Base Combined Prosthesis by 3D Printing
pmc-13233517.creator: Qingyu Xu, Yuxin Zhang, Xiang Wei, Liang Huo, Zixiang Han, Lingtong Bu, Minjie Chen, Jisi Zheng, Chi Yang
pmc-13233517.description: IntroductionThe combined lesions of the temporomandibular joint (TMJ) and skull base pose a considerable clinical challenge, frequently necessitating complex reconstructive procedures, yet established treatment protocols remain insufficient. This case series aims to assess the middle-term clinical safety, accuracy, and efficacy of our own customised temporomandibular joint-skull base combined prosthesis by 3D printing.

pmc-13407237.title: Expression of Anion Exchanger 1 (AE1) and Its Potential Involvement in Human Granulosa Cell Physiology: An In Vitro Pilot Study
pmc-13407237.creator: Loris Marin, Chiara Sabbadin, Claudia Maria Radu, Paola Brun, Carolina Frison, Giuseppe Gullo, Decio Armanini, Luciana Bordin, Eugenio Ragazzi, Guido Ambrosini, Alessandra Andrisani
pmc-13407237.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The anion exchanger 1 (AE1), traditionally known for its role in erythrocyte anion transport and acid–base homeostasis, has recently been identified in non-erythroid tissues, suggesting broader physiological functions. In the present study, we investigated for the first time the expression and potential role of AE1 in human ovarian granulosa cells (GCs) obtained from women with endometriosis (ENDO-GCs) or male factor infertility controls (MF-GCs).

pmc-13501104.title: Precision Dosing for Pediatric Growth Hormone Deficiency With Daily and Weekly Growth Hormone
pmc-13501104.creator: Wei Wu, Chun‐Xiu Gong, Jie Mei, Ling Hou, Yan Liang, Yan‐qin Ying, Feng Ye, Ge‐Hang Ju, Hui‐Xiang Tian, Nan Yang, Yun Qin, Dongsheng Ouyang, Xiaoping Luo
pmc-13501104.description: Pediatric growth hormone deficiency (GHD) typically requires daily injections of recombinant human growth hormone (rhGH). Long‐acting PEGylated recombinant human growth hormone (PEG‐rhGH) formulations have been developed to reduce injection frequency and improve adherence and quality of life. However, guidance on switching between short‐acting and long‐acting regimens during treatment and biomarker‐driven precision dose‐conversion strategies remains lacking in real‐world clinical practice.

(a) United States statutes to prevail in conflict No provision of any trade agreement approved by the Congress under section 2503(a) of this title, nor the application of any such provision to any person or circumstance, which is in conflict with any statute.
